extracted.intended_audience: aspiring stand-up comedians seeking to get passed at New York City comedy clubs
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, club-by-club advice on routes and requirements for being 'passed' (booked) at New York City comedy clubs, aimed at comics who have been working open mics and want paid/guest spots. Covers referrals, tapes, auditions, open-mic pipelines, producing, internships, and other entry paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be able to 'hold your own' / match level of laughs
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you match the level of laughs the lineup comics are getting if it were you up there?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit the club you want to get passed at and watch the comics on the lineup to assess whether your material and performance level are comparable. Clubs groom new talent but expect a reasonable level of consistency between comics; avoid following a killer if you can't hold your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong credits (late night TV) help but are not necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Having a strong credit like a late night TV credit helps get you in, but it is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a late night credit, get a friend who is a regular to recommend you and send your late-night tape. The author notes she got passed at every NYC club (except one) without such a credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referrals from trusted regulars carry weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations from trusted club regulars often matter for audition/passing decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't have a big credit, secure referrals from regulars at the club—these recommendations frequently influence bookers and can lead to auditions or guest spots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a strong tape to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'nice hot tape of yours killing on late night' or similar strong recording is useful when being recommended or submitting to a booker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bookers often want to see tapes; if a regular or famous comic recommends you, be ready to provide a recording that demonstrates your material and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy Cellar: recommendation requirement / audition process
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally requires recommendations from TWO Comedy Cellar regulars, OR one famous comedian recommendation, to get an audition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recently a regular (Sherrod Small) has been bringing comedians to the General Manager on Monday New Joke Night; if the GM likes you she may pass your tape to the Booker for an audition. Sherrod is willing to give honest readiness feedback to comics who ask.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standup NY: 'hang out' networking route
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting in is often a matter of 'hang out hang out hang out'—be present, get to know people, and let them know you're a comic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a bar outside the showroom where comics hang out; this networking method has worked for some, though the author found it an unreliable use of time and prefers other routes. A chance social connection led to sending a tape to the booker in the author's experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Comedy Mob open mic as scouting/booker pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy Mob mics are scouted by bookers and the Comedy Mob actually books check spots at Stand Up NY and New York Comedy Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend or perform at Comedy Mob mics (www.comedymob.com) because the hosts (George and Kevin) scout talent and can get comics seen by bookers—'2 for the price of 1' since you can be seen for multiple clubs.

rubrics_metrics.name: New York Comedy Club auditions (check status and call)
rubrics_metrics.description: NYCC had an audition process prior to the pandemic but it may be on hold; check with the club periodically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call the club to ask when auditions resume. Typically comics get passed for late night first (5-minute sets after the main show).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadway Comedy Club: bringer audition and residency opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadway Comedy Club runs a bringer audition (via the Industry Room) with the potential to win a 2-month residency on a pro show once a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Gordon at the Industry Room (theindustryroom.com). Even if you don't win the 2-month residency, mini residencies (one month) or guest spots may be awarded. The residency can lead to regular rotation bookings and provides valuable experience and a strong tape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greenwich Village Comedy Club: shared booker with Broadway
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the pandemic the GVCC booker is also the booker of Broadway Comedy Club, so getting seen at Industry Room shows can help entry to both clubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performing where the booker watches (e.g., Industry Room) increases chances of being noticed and passed for multiple clubs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic Strip Live: annual lottery/audition (check for reinstatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comic Strip Live used to run a yearly lottery where comedians line up to get an audition date; status may be paused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call the club to check if they will reinstate the lottery. Also, individual bringer shows/run by local producers (e.g., Kim Donat) can lead to recommendations to the booker.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Side Comedy Club: booker-run open mics and New Talent shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Felicia Madison (the booker) runs open mics and New Talent shows where performers can be seen and potentially passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Friday noon open mic is a recommended chance to be seen by the booker; sign up via the club's open mics calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing a show at a club is a route to entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Many clubs allow external producers to produce shows at their venue; producing can be an avenue to get into a club's rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can cold-pitch producing opportunities to clubs or ask an existing fellow producer for an introduction. Some comics were booked into rotations because of producing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internships may provide stage time in exchange for work
rubrics_metrics.description: Some clubs offer internships (often seating people) that grant 5 minutes of stage time in exchange for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadway Comedy Club has an internship program; check with other clubs (but likely NOT Gotham, the Cellar, or the Stand) to see if they offer similar opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barking (promoting shows) as a way to get stage time (Grisly Pear example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs like The Grisly Pear give comedians the chance to 'bark' (get people to attend) in exchange for stage time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the club (e.g., grislypearstandup.com) for details; barking can be a practical trade to secure stage time and gain exposure.
